H5277.name: Naam
H5277.brief: Son of Caleb, from the tribe of Judah.
H5277.short: Naam was a son of Caleb, mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah in 1 Chronicles.

H5279A.name: Naamah
H5279A.desc: Woman living at the time of United Monarchy
H5279A.brief: An Ammonite; mother of King Rehoboam of Judah.
H5279A.short: Naamah, an Ammonite woman, was the mother of Rehoboam, who succeeded his father Solomon as king of Judah.

H5279G.name: Naamah
H5279G.desc: Woman living at the time before the Flood
H5279G.brief: Daughter of Lamech and Zillah, sister of Tubal-cain.
H5279G.short: Naamah was the daughter of Lamech and Zillah, and the sister of Tubal-cain, mentioned in the genealogy of Cain.

H5283J.name: Naaman
H5283J.brief: A descendant of Benjamin, son of Ehud.
H5283J.short: Naaman, a descendant of Benjamin, was one of the sons of Ehud mentioned in the genealogy of 1 Chronicles.

H5283I.name: Naaman
H5283I.desc: Syrian living at the time of Divided Monarchy
H5283I.brief: Aramean commander healed of leprosy by Elisha.
H5283I.short: Naaman, a commander of the Aramean army, was healed of his leprosy by the prophet Elisha, demonstrating God's power and compassion.

H5283G.name: Naaman
H5283G.desc: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
H5283G.short: Naaman, also known as Nohah, was one of the sons of Benjamin mentioned in the genealogies of Genesis and 1 Chronicles.

H5283H.name: Naaman
H5283H.desc: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
H5283H.brief: Grandson of Benjamin, head of the Naamite clan.
H5283H.short: Naaman, a grandson of Benjamin through Bela, was the head of the Naamite clan within the tribe of Benjamin.

H5284.name: Naamathites
H5284.brief: The people group of Zophar, Job's friend.
H5284.short: The Naamathites were the people group to which Zophar, one of Job's three friends, belonged.

H5292B.name: Naarah
H5292B.desc: Woman living at the time of Divided Monarchy
H5292B.brief: Wife of Ashhur, the founder of Tekoa.
H5292B.short: Naarah was one of the two wives of Ashhur, the  father (ie founder) of Tekoa, mentioned in the genealogy of Judah.

H5293.name: Naarai
H5293.desc: Warrior living at the time of Divided Monarchy
H5293.brief: One of David's mighty warriors, son of Ezbai.
H5293.short: Naarai, the son of Ezbai, was one of the mighty warriors who fought alongside King David.

H5225.name: Nacon
H5225.desc: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
H5225.brief: Threshing floor where Uzzah touched the ark.
H5225.short: Nacon, also known as Chidon, was the owner of the threshing floor where Uzzah touched the ark of God and was struck down.

H5281.name: Naomi
H5281.short: Naomi, also known as Mara, was an Israelite woman who, after losing her husband and sons, returned from Moab to Bethlehem with her daughter-in-law Ruth.

H5294G.name: Neariah
H5294G.desc: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
H5294G.brief: Descendant of David, son of Shemaiah.
H5294G.short: Neariah, a descendant of King David, was the son of Shemaiah and had three sons: Elioenai, Hizkiah, and Azrikam.

H5294H.name: Neariah
H5294H.desc: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
H5294H.brief: A Simeonite leader who defeated the Amalekites.
H5294H.short: Neariah, along with other Simeonite leaders, defeated the remaining Amalekites during the reign of King Hezekiah.

H5224G.name: Neco
H5224G.desc: Pharaoh living at the time of Divided Monarchy
H5224G.brief: Egyptian Pharaoh during the reigns of Josiah and Jehoiakim.
H5224G.short: Pharaoh Neco II, the ruler of Egypt, opposed King Josiah of Judah, installed Jehoiakim as a vassal king, and was later defeated by Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon.

H5241G.name: Nemuel
H5241G.desc: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
H5241G.brief: Son of Eliab, from the tribe of Reuben.
H5241G.short: Nemuel was a son of Eliab and a member of the tribe of Reuben.

H5298H.name: Nepheg
H5298H.desc: David's son living at the time of United Monarchy
H5298H.brief: Son of King David, born in Jerusalem.
H5298H.short: Nepheg was one of the sons of King David, born to him in Jerusalem.

H5298G.name: Nepheg
H5298G.desc: Levite living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
H5298G.brief: Son of Izhar, from the tribe of Levi.
H5298G.short: Nepheg was a son of Izhar and a member of the Levite clan of Kohath.

H5248.name: Nimrod
H5248.desc: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
H5248.short: Nimrod was a mighty hunter and ruler who built several notable cities, including Babel and Nineveh.

H5250.name: Nimshi
H5250.desc: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
H5250.short: Nimshi was the grandfather of Jehu, the king of Israel who overthrew the dynasty of Ahab.

H5270.name: Noah
H5270.desc: Woman living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
H5270.short: Noah was one of the daughters of Zelophehad who received an inheritance in the Promised Land.

H5297.name: Memphis
H5297.brief: An important city in ancient Egypt
H5297.short: Memphis, an ancient Egyptian city mentioned in prophecies of judgment against Egypt (<ref="Isaiah 19:13; Jeremiah 2:16; 44:1; 46:14, 19; Ezk.30.13, 16; Hosea 9:6">Isaiah 19:13; Jeremiah 2:16; 44:1; 46:14, 19; Ezk.30.13, 16; Hosea 9:6</ref>).

H5279B.name: Naamah
H5279B.brief: A town in the Judean lowlands
H5279B.short: Naamah was a town in the Judean lowlands, mentioned in the tribal allotment of Judah.

H5295.name: Naaran
H5295.brief: A border town between Ephraim and Benjamin
H5295.short: Naaran, also called Naarah, was a border town between the tribes of Ephraim and Benjamin.

H5272.name: Neah
H5272.brief: A border town of Zebulun and Asher
H5272.short: Neah, also called Neiel, was a border town between the territories of Zebulun and Asher.

H5249.name: Nimrim
H5249.brief: A place in Moab known for its waters
H5249.short: Nimrim was a place in Moab known for its waters, which are mentioned in the context of God's judgment on Moab.

H5210.name: Nineveh
H5210.brief: The capital of Assyria, known for its wickedness and repentance
H5210.short: Nineveh, the capital of Assyria, is known in the Bible for its wickedness and its remarkable repentance following Jonah's preaching.

H5268.name: Nisroch
H5268.brief: An Assyrian deity, possibly associated with agriculture
H5268.short: Nisroch, mentioned in <ref="2Ki.19.37; Isaiah 37:38">2Ki.19.37; Isaiah 37:38</ref>, was an Assyrian deity in whose temple King Sennacherib was worshipping when he was assassinated by his sons.
